doc.title: Billy Bauer interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998

chapter: Metronome All Stars and Charlie Parker
title: Phil Schaap, Jimmy Hall and writing a book
summary: Phil Schaap questioned his facts, and Bauer urges Rowe and everybody to keep a diary or write a book.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Yeah wait a minute, that’s what Phil Schaap says. I was talking to him and we got going, and he says, “I’m going to look that up,” he says, “you’ve got me worried.” He says, “I used to think I knew everything, but when you questioned it—” and that same program after I got back, Jimmy Hall rang me up, and he says, “Me and my wife were out in the country and I heard you being interviewed.” He says, “Man,” he says, “when I was being interviewed, this guy would get me so wrapped up I couldn’t talk.” He knew everything. He says he was getting it.
Well maybe it’s time for another book, huh?
No, one is enough. I’ve got a lot of things I could—
What do you think is the—
Why don’t you write a book?
I think it will. Especially after today.

You should. Everybody should. Everybody should. You know like I tell the guys I says make a diary, every day. I’ve got a little machine, you know, you just, when you think of a story just tell the machine. And at the end of a week or so, copy all of them down. That’s what I more or less did.
You’ll have a lot of material in a hurry, yeah.
Well I just kept on putting it down on a little cassette or something. You should. You’ve got a great name, Monk.
